name: maxwell-v2
summary: Applies Maxwell filtering (SSS, or tSSS when a buffer duration is set) to Elekta/MEGIN MEG raw data with MNE-Python, with optional automatic noisy/flat channel detection, and outputs the filtered raw FIF.
description: Loads the raw MEG file, optionally detects noisy and flat channels with find_bad_channels_maxwell, then runs mne.preprocessing.maxwell_filter with the given origin, temporal SSS settings and magnetometer scaling, writing the result and QC figures. Use it as an early MEG preprocessing step for MEGIN/Elekta data. Fine-calibration and cross-talk files are taken from the input when present; otherwise the calibration and cross-talk files bundled in the repository are used, which belong to a specific scanner and may not match yours. The App stops if the data were already Maxwell filtered.

inputs.description: Raw MEG recording (Elekta/MEGIN FIF) not yet Maxwell filtered.

outputs.description: Maxwell-filtered raw MEG data in FIF format.

parameters.description: Detect noisy and flat channels with find_bad_channels_maxwell and mark them bad before filtering. The registered parameter id ends with a tab character while the code reads 'auto_bad_channels', so the default (true) is always used.
Buffer length in seconds for temporal SSS (tSSS); empty for spatial SSS only.
Correlation limit between inner and outer subspaces used to reject components in tSSS.
Origin of the SSS expansion: 'auto' or comma-separated x,y,z coordinates.
Scaling applied to magnetometers relative to gradiometers (number or 'auto').

citations.text: Gramfort A. et al. MEG and EEG data analysis with MNE-Python. Frontiers in Neuroscience 7:267 (2013).

failure_modes.message: FATAL: Maxwell filtering already applied to this data.
failure_modes.fix: Use the raw data before Maxwell filtering.

failure_modes.message: FATAL: No MEG FIF file found. Set 'fif' in config.json.
failure_modes.fix: Connect a raw MEG FIF input.
